title: claim() / stake() / withdraw() violate checks-effects-interactions: _claimRewards's external phUSD.mint + rewardToken.safeTransfer happen BEFORE debts are rebased and BEFORE principal accounting is updated; cross-function reentrancy enables double-claim and (for withdraw) corrupted totalStaked if either token has a callback
function: claim / stake / withdraw (shared root in _claimRewards external calls)
rootCause: Three reward-bearing entrypoints (`claim`, `stake`, `withdraw`) call `_claimRewards` (which performs `phUSD.mint(user, ...)` and `rewardToken.safeTransfer(user, ...)`) BEFORE rebasing `user.phUSDDebt`/`user.stableDebt` and BEFORE updating `user.amount`/`totalStaked`. None of these functions carry `nonReentrant` (only `collectReward` does). If `phUSD.mint` exposes a callback (extension to IFlax) or `rewardToken` is a hooked ERC20 (e.g. ERC777), the recipient can re-enter `claim`/`stake`/`withdraw` while debts are still anchored to pre-claim values; the inner call re-pays the same pending amount. For `withdraw`, the inner call also passes the `user.amount >= amount` check against the un-decremented stake, corrupting `totalStaked` accounting after the outer call completes.
trustAssumption: Reachability is gated by trust assumption profile §10: phUSD.mint is non-callback AND rewardToken is a non-hooked vanilla ERC20. If governance ever points rewardToken at an ERC777 / mint-hook token, the exploit is live. Even under the assumption, the cheap fix (`nonReentrant`) removes the contingent risk surface.
impactSummary: Conditional on the trust assumption: double-claim of pending rewards (drains rewardBalance and inflates phUSD supply); for withdraw, additional totalStaked corruption that under-counts after outer-after-inner sequencing. Compound effect: attacker can withdraw more principal than they hold AND extract multiple reward payouts in a single transaction.
preservedDetails: CODE-004/005/006 each carry the strongest narrative for their respective entrypoint (concrete attack vector, line-by-line ordering). PATTERN-001/002/003 add the pattern-DB structural framing (REENTRANCY-ERC777). SLITHER-003/004/005 (reentrancy-no-eth) and SLITHER-007/008/009 (reentrancy-events) provide the raw SAST confirmation. CODE-006 carries the most damaging variant (totalStaked corruption beyond double-claim).
remediation: Add `nonReentrant` to `stake`, `withdraw`, and `claim`. Belt-and-braces: rebase `user.{phUSD,stable}Debt` INSIDE `_claimRewards` BEFORE the `phUSD.mint`/`rewardToken.safeTransfer` external calls. Shared single fix across all three entrypoints.
consolidationRationale: Root cause (debt rebase happens after external mint+transfer) and remediation (nonReentrant + CEI reorder) are identical across the three entrypoints. Slither's reentrancy-no-eth and reentrancy-events firings on the same three functions are the SAST shadow of the same defect. PATTERN-001/002/003 confirm the structural REENTRANCY-ERC777 signature. Single cluster with three instances is the cleanest expression; report-writer may still split into 3 submissions if entrypoint-specific PoCs are required, but the dedup ledger keeps them as one unit.
dedupNotes: Collapsed 12 raw findings (3 CODE + 3 PATTERN + 6 SLITHER) into one cluster with 3 instances. SLITHER-007/008/009 (reentrancy-events at Low) are subsumed because the underlying reentrancy windows are already captured by the higher-severity reentrancy-no-eth findings on the same lines.
